symptoms: The bug damages new shoots and leaves.
It causes damage to the flower clusters.
It leads to the loss of young, tender nuts.
The bug feeds on plant tissues and causes blight.
favourable_conditions: The bug thrives in temperatures between 24 and 32 degrees Celsius with relative humidity between 50 and 100 percent.
prevention: Remove alternate host plants like neem, guava, cocoa, and cotton from your farm.
Clear out self-sown neem plants in and around the plantation.
Avoid planting cashew near other crops that host these bugs, such as cotton.
Work with your neighbors to manage the pest on a large community scale.
practices: Monitor your crop regularly to look for signs of damage.
Count and record the number of nymphs and adults on five random twigs per plant.
